subject: Maths
title: Best value problems
subtitle: Ratio · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can compare unit prices to determine which product offers the best value.

key_vocab.definition: finding which option gives you the most for your money. Compare by finding the price per unit (or amount per penny).
Divide price by quantity to find cost per unit. The lowest unit price is the best value.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can compare unit prices to determine which product offers the best value.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content:
Best value -- finding which option gives you the most for your money. Compare by finding the price per unit (or amount per penny).
Method -- Divide price by quantity to find cost per unit. The lowest unit price is the best value.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Calculate the cost per unit for each option. The one with the lowest unit cost is the best value.
Unit price = &frac{cost}{quantity}
Compare unit prices: lowest = best value

Key examples:
  ✓ 500ml for £2 = 0.4p/ml  (price per ml)
  ✓ 750ml for £2.70 = 0.36p/ml  (cheaper per ml)
  ✓ Lower unit price = better value  (comparison rule)
  ✗ The cheapest item is always best value  (must compare unit price)
  ✗ Bigger is always better value  (not necessarily)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – two sizes
  Juice: 500ml for £1.20 or 1.5L for £3.00. Which is better value?
  Small: 120p ÷ 500 = 0.24p per ml
  Large: 300p ÷ 1500 = 0.20p per ml
  Large is cheaper per ml
  1.5L is better value
  (Compare price per ml to find the best deal.)

Example 2 – three options
  Cereal: 400g for £2.80, 750g for £4.50, 1kg for £6.50. Best value?
  400g: 280 ÷ 400 = 0.70p/g
  750g: 450 ÷ 750 = 0.60p/g
  1kg: 650 ÷ 1000 = 0.65p/g
  750g is best value (0.60p/g)
  (The biggest size is not always the best value.)

sections.title: Comparing two sizes
sections.content:
Find the unit price and state which is better value.

(a) Water: 500ml for 80p or 1.5L for £2.10
(b) Rice: 1kg for £1.80 or 2kg for £3.20
(c) Pasta: 500g for £1.35 or 1kg for £2.50
(d) Soap: 3 bars for £1.50 or 8 bars for £3.60

sections.title: Three options
sections.content:
Find the best value from three options.

(a) Juice: 250ml £0.60, 500ml £1.10, 1L £1.90
(b) Crisps: 25g 50p, 50g 85p, 150g £2.10
(c) Eggs: 6 for £1.50, 10 for £2.30, 15 for £3.60
(d) Pens: 3 for £2.40, 5 for £3.75, 10 for £7.00

sections.title: With offers and discounts
sections.content:
Include the offer in your calculation.

(a) A: £3.60 for 6, B: £4.80 for 8 with 25% off. Better value?
(b) A: 2L for £2.20, B: 3L for £3.60 buy-one-get-one-free. Better value?
(c) A: 500g at £4.00, B: 750g at £5.40 with 10% off. Better value?
(d) A: 12 pack £6, B: 20 pack £9 with buy 2 get 1 free. Better value?

sections.title: Real-world best value
sections.content:
Solve each best value problem.

(a) Taxi A: £3 + £1.50/km. Taxi B: £5 + £1.00/km. Which is cheaper for 8 km?
(b) Phone plan A: £15/month + 5p/text. B: £20/month unlimited. Crossover texts?
(c) Petrol A: 145.9p/L. Petrol B: 142.5p/L but 3 miles further. Saving on 40L?
(d) Gym A: £30/month. Gym B: £5 per visit. Break-even visits per month?

sections.title: Mixed best value
sections.content:
Determine the best value option.

(a) Shampoo: 200ml £2.50, 400ml £4.20, 500ml £5.50
(b) Dog food: 400g £1.60, 1.2kg £4.20, 2kg £7.50
(c) Cinema: adult £12, family (2+2) £38, 5-ticket bundle £50
(d) Internet: 30GB for £15 or unlimited for £22. Use 50GB. Which?
(e) Paint: 1L for £8, 2.5L for £18, 5L for £32. Need 4L. Cheapest option?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Best value means lowest unit price
✗ The biggest pack is always best value
✓ To compare, divide price by quantity
✗ The cheapest total price is always the best value
✓ Buy-one-get-one-free halves the unit price
